one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event in the window: Q3 FY2027 results (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected around Nov 18-25 (last year 2025-11-19; date not yet announced as of 11-02). Guide: revenue $1.90-1.98B, adjusted EBITDA $281-302M, adjusted EPS $4.33-4.79; Street (Zacks) 4.33 sits at the low end, whisper 4.55 (80% range 4.24-4.88). The company beat its EPS midpoint in each of the last 6 quarters (median +15%) and our build gives ~5.22, so a beat is likely, but the August beat-and-raise was followed by a 17% two-week drop: the stock is trading on FY28 Communications visibility (wireless recapture, AT&T lowering 2027-28 capital investment on 10-21, the day DY made new lows) rather than on the quarter. Also in the window: Census construction spending (Dec 1). Setting: median +2% (likely beat, after a 61% drawdown from the 52-week high to near the low) with a 16% one-month sigma (53%/3.5 = 15% plus an earnings-day premium); kept near symmetric because the reaction to beats has been poor.

reasoning: Primary lane. Started from the filings and releases: Q2 FY27 beat (revenue 2,006, adjusted EBITDA 315.5, adjusted EPS 5.29) but Communications was cut ~$150M for a wireless deferral into FY28 and its margin guided to a slight decline (Ex.99.1, call). Scored six quarters of guidance: revenue beat the midpoint 5 of 6 (median +5.0%), EBITDA 6 of 6 (+8.8%), EPS 6 of 6 (+14.9%); FY26 annual guide beaten by 5.8%. The 10-Q shows the supplier finance program (367.4 obligations, built from zero since Q4 FY26) and customer concentration (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3%). New primary evidence the recaps skip: AT&T on 2026-10-21 lowered its 2027-28 capital investment outlook to $22-23B a year (8-K Ex.99.1), the day DY hit new lows; three insiders bought in September at $281-297 (Form 4s); a director resigned without disagreement (8-K 08-25); Census data-center construction was $96.5B SAAR in Sep-26 (+90% y/y). We use the approved driver set unchanged (base EPS NTM at horizon ~$22.9 vs Street ~21.5, +6.5%: the drivers sit above the guide on the record) and put our disagreement (AT&T capex -> slower FY28-29 backlog, ~-$11 a share) in gap_note and the downside case. Value: P/E 13.2x (peer median 18.65x shrunk to own 12.1x at k=0.8) and EV/EBITDA 9.5x; base $306.70 (+39% vs $221.05). Downside (P10) $143 moves backlog -12%, Communications margin -2pt, BS share -25%, BS margin -3pt and the multiple -2.5 turns; upside (P90) $496 moves backlog +8%, margin +1pt, BS share +20%, multiple +3.5. The left tail is wider in log terms, reflecting customer concentration. Limitations: no NTM EBITDA consensus for peers; only four whole-company peers; Twelve Data fundamentals were unavailable; no option data used. Every leg is driver-linked.

model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) supplier finance program counted 50% debt-like (+/- $6.1 a share); (2) P/E exit k=0.8 (default); (3) AT&T lowered 2027-28 capital investment (new primary evidence after the driver set was built): we would trim FY28-29 Communications backlog growth to ~6% a year (engine: about -$11 a share, -3.5%) but kept the approved driver values. Method-fit flag (thin XBRL) does not bite: DY files full XBRL (TTM revenue F6), so standard methods hold. No financing event at >=20% probability (net leverage ~2.3x, revolver availability $746.4M).
